Now being an Oklahoma native I feel that we (Okie's) have a unique perspective upon how to explain them.

I have been near a great many of them and learned some things about them. So here is some words.

The first thing you will notice about 30 minutes before the event is that the clouds overhead will change shape. If you are in a plains state such as Oklahoma you will see what is referee to as a wall cloud. It is called this because of its encompassing magnitude. The cloud will be very low to the ground. The lower and larger (they will extend really high up as well) doesn't mean you are in for it either.

The air will feel different as well. I don't care if you have never been within a storm capable of producing a tornado you will feel the change I am speaking of. The rest of this you will need to put all that shit you saw on "Twister" out of your mind.

The moments before a tornado the sky will almost always take on a green hue. The animals will go quiet and the wind will stop. That bullshit of how it will rain and hail before a tornado is just that. Bullshit! Often times the tornados will be what is called rain wrapped. That means the funnel will be masked by the rain.

Now tornados are not wedge shaped either. They usually have this rope appearance. A good rule of thumb is that if you can see the rotation in the clouds its a safe bet you are proper fucked and it will come down very near your location. What makes a tornado visible is the debris kicked up from the suction. This is the actual bad part.

That debris is fucking devastating. I have seen blades of grass embedded into utility poles or fence posts thru concrete curbs. Cars literally wrapped around a tree. The wind is like nothing you can ever imagine. The imbalance of air pressure will cause some of the most fucked things to happen.

There is only one safe place when you are in the path of one. Underground.

Now the scales of tornados are somewhat useful to know, but most cases they are assessed after they tear thru shit.

F-1 these are going to take the shingles off your roof and knock down some branches.

F-2 these will take the siding off your home. Pick up larger objects and toss them around.

F-3 these are where you need to worry about your life. They will level a home. Cause a trailer to explode. Flip cars and snap fairly robust trees at around 9 to 15 feet. They will clear the bark off a tree with ease and throw shit everywhere.

F-4 these will usually be in that wedge shape. They will often times be as wide as a football field. These are also powerful enough to uproot large trees. They can pick up a car and throw it. They will cause utter devastation as well.

F-5 This is the top of the scale. You might as well pray to your god if you didn't have enough time to get away. I have seen one in my life. May 3rd 1999. Fellow Okie's can chime in for this.

This was the worse thing I have ever seen. Being an Oklahoman we are accustomed to getting fucked up. Our weathermen and women (Emily Sutton is a saint and Gary England is a fucking legend) are extremely professional when relaying the information available.

Not that day. I saw Gary England cry.....this tornado tore a path from Lawton up the HE Bailey turnpike and into Kansas. When it hit Moore it was like nothing Oklahoma or the world had seen to that point.

It was over a mile wide. The tornado had just intensified to a F-5 as well. It went past the theater in Moore and tore right thru a housing division. Gary said on the air that if you are in the path and able to hear his voice he wished there was more he could do. It bore down and dug a hole almost 6 feet deep in the ground there was nothing to be done but hope for the best and plan for the worse.

Homes were not leveled they were gone....just gone. The tornado also spawned what are called sisters that rotate around the main funnel. This happened as it was halfway into Moore. When it crossed I-35 it took part of the highway with it. There was debris all up and down the highway. When the dust cleared and emergency crews went in there was nothing really left.

That day the planet showed what it was capable of. There had been and still happen to be tragic storms that devastate communities. This took it. Just fucking took it and it didn't care.

Lots of things happened because of that tornado as well. Improved radar for tracking. The weather prediction center in Norman is unmatched. They can zoom in to street level. They can see the smoke from wild fires. As a matter of fact in 2009 they did just that. Channel 4 and 9 were directing fire efforts to locations shown on doppler radar to smoke.

Things to remember if you happen to be unfortunate enough to witness a tornado.

If its getting bigger it is getting closer.

If you are in its path get to the lowest and center most part of your house.
